categories.grounded: Ask is fully answerable from the corpus — crew should cite sections, no assumptions needed beyond PM-level calls
categories.partially_grounded: Some corpus context exists, but the ask spans beyond it — crew must ground what it can and flag what it can't
categories.ungrounded: No corpus context — crew must flag everything as assumption, use PLACEHOLDER pattern
categories.scope_trap: Ask invites scope creep or contains 'and' that implies multiple stories — crew should stay narrow or flag the split
categories.adversarial: Ask is vague, contradictory, or tests failure-mode defenses — crew should handle gracefully

meta.scoring_guide: LLM-as-judge scores each dimension 1-5. Reference stories are the anchor, not the ceiling — a crew output that improves on the reference is fine. The rubric judges the output against the reference on each dimension independently.

golden_set.ask: Users keep missing when their saved jobs get reposted. We should notify them somehow.
expected_behaviors: Researcher cites saved_jobs table (C1), repost detection via features view (C3), no notification infra (C4), and icebox digest item (C6)
Analyst scopes to email notification only — push/in-app out of scope (no infra exists per C4)
Analyst flags daily batch latency as a constraint from C3
Writer produces AC/ACE format with specific role 'job seeker' not bare 'user'
Assumptions include channel choice and daily cap value as PM calls

reference_story.title: Saved Jobs – Repost Notification Email
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to receive an email when a job I saved is reposted, so that I can decide whether it's still worth applying to.

acs.name: Repost Notification Sent
acs.given: a job seeker has a saved job that is detected as reposted
thens: The job seeker will receive one email per repost event.
The email will link back to the posting with its current ghost-score.

acs.name: Daily Cap Reached
acs.given: a job seeker has reached the daily notification cap
acs.when: further repost events are detected that day
thens: The additional events will be held and included in the next day's email.

acs.name: Job Unsaved Before Check
acs.given: a job seeker unsaved the job before the daily check runs
acs.when: repost detection fires for that posting
thens: No notification will be sent for that job.

acs.name: Posting Deleted
acs.given: a saved job's posting is deleted after a repost is detected
thens: The item will be omitted from the email.
A skip event will be logged with user ID, posting ID, and timestamp (UTC).

assumptions_carried: A1 — Email is the right channel; no channel-preference data exists.
A2 — Daily cadence is acceptable given batch ingest.
A3 — Cap value (N emails/day) is a PM call, not derivable from data.

golden_set.ask: We should show why a job got flagged as ghost.
expected_behaviors: Researcher cites the three deterministic signals in features.sql (C2) and GUARDRAILS.md evidence panel call (C5)
Analyst scopes to Analyze page evidence panel — not Browse page, not appeal flow
Writer ACs reference specific signals (repost frequency, posting age, cross-board spread) by name
ACE covers signal unavailable / no history case

reference_story.title: Analyze – Ghost-Flag Evidence Panel
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to see the evidence behind a ghost flag, so that I can judge for myself whether to trust the score.

acs.name: Evidence Displayed
acs.given: a job seeker has analyzed a posting
thens: The three deterministic signals will be shown with their values alongside the verdict.
The model's rationale will be displayed in full without truncation.

acs.name: Missing Signal
acs.given: a posting has no history for one of the signals
thens: The signal will be shown as "No history" rather than omitted.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Evidence shows for both GHOST and REAL verdicts, not just GHOST.
A2 — Signal values are shown raw, not normalized.

golden_set.ask: Let people snooze a saved job instead of deleting it.
expected_behaviors: Researcher identifies saved_jobs is binary today with no status field (C1)
Analyst identifies schema migration as a dependency
Analyst flags interaction with repost notifications if G01 is also built
Writer ACs cover snooze applied, snooze expires, and job closes while snoozed
Assumptions include preset durations as a PM call

reference_story.title: Saved Jobs – Snooze a Saved Job
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to snooze a saved job for a set period, so that I can keep my saved list focused without losing track of postings I might return to.

acs.name: Snooze Applied
acs.given: a job seeker is viewing a saved job
acs.when: they select "Snooze" and a preset duration
thens: The job will be hidden from the default saved list until the snooze expires.
The job will appear under the "Snoozed" filter with its wake date.

acs.name: Snooze Expires
acs.given: a snoozed job's duration elapses
thens: The job will return to the saved list marked "Returned from snooze".

acs.name: Job Closes While Snoozed
acs.given: a job closes while it is snoozed
acs.when: the snooze expires and the job would return
thens: The job will return with a "Closed" indicator rather than silently disappearing.

acs.name: Snooze Then Unsave
acs.given: a job seeker has a snoozed job
thens: The snooze will be cancelled and the job removed from all saved views.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Presets of 1w / 2w / 1m are sufficient; custom durations out of scope.
A2 — Snoozed jobs are excluded from repost notifications; needs a product call.

golden_set.ask: The Browse page needs a way to filter out likely ghost jobs.
expected_behaviors: Researcher identifies that ghost-score exists but is only shown on Analyze page (C2)
Researcher cites calm UI / sensitivity context from C5 — filter should not be alarmist
Analyst scopes to a filter toggle on Browse — not removing ghost postings, filtering them
Writer frames the filter language per GUARDRAILS.md — e.g. 'Hide flagged postings' not 'Remove ghosts'
ACE covers edge case where all results are filtered out (empty state)

reference_story.title: Browse – Ghost Filter Toggle
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to filter out postings likely to be ghost jobs from Browse results, so that I can focus my time on real opportunities.

acs.name: Filter Toggle Available
acs.given: a job seeker is on the Browse page
thens: A toggle labeled "Hide flagged postings" will be visible in the filter bar.
The toggle will default to off.

acs.name: Filter Applied
acs.given: a job seeker enables the ghost filter toggle
thens: Postings with a ghost score at or above the threshold will be hidden.
A count of hidden postings will be shown (e.g. "12 flagged postings hidden").

acs.name: All Results Filtered
acs.given: a job seeker enables the ghost filter
acs.when: all results in the current view are above the threshold
thens: An empty state will be shown with the message "All results in this search are flagged — try adjusting your filters."

acs.name: Filter Persists Across Pages
acs.given: a job seeker has the ghost filter enabled
acs.when: they navigate to the next page of results
thens: The filter state will persist without requiring re-toggle.

assumptions_carried: A1 — The threshold for filtering matches the existing ghost-score threshold (not a separate setting).
A2 — Filter state is session-only; does not persist across logins.

golden_set.ask: We need a way for users to dispute a ghost score they think is wrong.
expected_behaviors: Researcher cites C5 (users can disagree with the model) but notes no dispute mechanism exists
Analyst scopes to a feedback submission — not a score override, not a recalculation
Analyst flags that the backend for handling disputes does not exist in the corpus — dependency
Writer does not invent a dispute-resolution workflow; flags it as assumption
Grounding score should reflect that the dispute backend is entirely ungrounded

reference_story.title: Analyze – Dispute Ghost Score
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to submit feedback when I believe a ghost score is wrong, so that the platform can improve its accuracy over time.

acs.name: Dispute Button Available
acs.given: a job seeker is viewing an analyzed posting
thens: A "Report inaccuracy" link will be visible below the evidence panel.

acs.name: Dispute Submitted
acs.given: a job seeker clicks "Report inaccuracy"
acs.when: they select a reason and submit
thens: A confirmation message will be shown: "Thanks — your feedback helps improve our scoring."
The dispute will be logged with posting ID, user ID, reason, and timestamp (UTC).

acs.name: Duplicate Dispute
acs.given: a job seeker has already submitted a dispute for this posting
thens: The button will be replaced with "Feedback submitted" and no duplicate will be created.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Disputes are logged for review; they do not trigger an immediate score change.
A2 — Dispute reasons are a preset list (e.g. 'I was contacted', 'Company confirmed role is open', 'Other') — not free text.
A3 — No dispute-review workflow exists; backend handling is a separate story.

golden_set.ask: Job seekers should be able to export their saved jobs as a CSV.
expected_behaviors: Researcher cites saved_jobs table and History page (C1) but notes no export functionality exists
Analyst scopes to CSV export of saved jobs only — not analyzed results, not application history
Analyst flags that export column schema is a PM decision (assumption)
Writer ACs cover the download trigger, file contents, and empty-state edge case

reference_story.title: Saved Jobs – CSV Export
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to export my saved jobs as a CSV file, so that I can track my job search outside the platform.

acs.name: Export Button Available
acs.given: a job seeker is on the History page with saved jobs
thens: An "Export CSV" button will be visible in the page header.

acs.name: CSV Downloaded
acs.given: a job seeker clicks "Export CSV"
thens: A CSV file will be downloaded containing one row per saved job.
Columns will include: job title, company, date saved, ghost score, and posting URL.

acs.name: No Saved Jobs
acs.given: a job seeker has no saved jobs
thens: The "Export CSV" button will be hidden or disabled.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Column schema (title, company, date saved, ghost score, URL) is assumed; PM to confirm.
A2 — Export includes all saved jobs, not a filtered subset.

golden_set.ask: We should add a referral program so users can invite friends.
expected_behaviors: Researcher finds no relevant context — returns a single bullet stating this
Analyst flags everything as assumption (A1, A2, A3, ...)
Writer uses PLACEHOLDER pattern throughout — bracketed placeholders for role, reward structure, etc.
Story should still be structurally valid (AC/ACE format, GIVEN/WHEN/THEN) even though content is ungrounded
Grounding score should be LOW — this is the correct behavior

reference_story.title: [Feature Name] – Referral Program (PLACEHOLDER)
reference_story.story: As a [role to be confirmed], I want to invite friends to AutoApply via a referral link, so that [outcome to be confirmed by PM].

acs.name: Referral Link Generated (Assumed)
acs.given: a [role to be confirmed] is on their account page
thens: A unique referral link will be generated and displayed.
The link will be copyable to clipboard.

acs.name: Review Gate
acs.given: this story was generated without grounded context
thens: Assumptions A1–A4 will be resolved before the story is committed.

assumptions_carried: A1 — A referral program is the right growth mechanism; no user-research data exists.
A2 — Reward structure (credits, free months, etc.) is entirely a PM call.
A3 — No referral infrastructure exists; full backend is a separate epic.
A4 — The user role and benefit statement require PM confirmation.

expected_behaviors: Researcher finds no relevant context — maybe tangentially notes C5 UI principles but nothing about theming
Analyst scopes narrowly to a theme toggle — not a full design-system overhaul
Writer uses PLACEHOLDER for design-token specifics
Even though ungrounded, the story should be structurally complete

reference_story.title: [Feature Name] – Dark Mode Toggle (PLACEHOLDER)
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to switch to a dark color theme, so that I can use AutoApply comfortably in low-light settings.

acs.name: Toggle Available
acs.given: a job seeker is on any page
thens: A "Dark mode" toggle will be visible.
The current theme state will be indicated.

acs.name: Theme Applied
acs.given: a job seeker enables dark mode
thens: The UI will re-render with the dark color theme without a page reload.

acs.name: Preference Persists
acs.given: a job seeker has enabled dark mode
acs.when: they return in a new session
thens: The dark theme will be applied on load without requiring re-toggle.

assumptions_carried: A1 — No design tokens or theming infrastructure exists; implementation approach is a tech call.
A2 — Preference is stored per-user, not per-device.
A3 — All pages and components support dark mode; partial rollout is out of scope.

golden_set.ask: Users should be able to save jobs and get notified when similar ones appear.
expected_behaviors: The ask contains 'and' linking two distinct capabilities — save (exists per C1) and similarity matching (does not exist)
Analyst should either split into two stories or scope to one and move the other to out-of-scope
Writer's 'I want' clause must NOT contain 'and' — skill rule
If the crew handles it as one story, the self-check should warn about the compound WHEN or the broad scope

reference_story.title: Saved Jobs – Similar Job Alerts
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to receive alerts when new postings similar to my saved jobs appear, so that I can discover relevant opportunities without manual searching.

acs.name: Similar Job Detected
acs.given: a job seeker has saved jobs and new postings are ingested
thens: Postings above the similarity threshold will be identified per saved job.

acs.name: Alert Sent
acs.given: similar postings are found
thens: The job seeker will receive one email listing up to 5 similar postings per saved job.
Each item will show the job title, company, and similarity reason.

acs.name: No Similar Jobs Found
acs.given: no postings meet the similarity threshold
thens: No alert will be sent for that day.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Saving already exists (C1); this story covers the alert capability only.
A2 — Similarity matching does not exist; the algorithm and threshold are a separate spike.
A3 — Email is the alert channel (same assumption as repost notifications).
A4 — Daily cadence matches batch ingest (C3).

golden_set.notes: The reference story scopes to alerts only and moves save to out-of-scope (it already exists). The crew should recognize the compound ask and not produce a story with 'and' in the 'I want' clause.

golden_set.ask: Build a dashboard that shows analytics, trends, ghost score distribution, and application success rates.
expected_behaviors: The ask is a kitchen-sink feature — 4+ capabilities in one sentence
Analyst should flag this as too broad and suggest splitting into multiple stories
If the Writer proceeds, the happy-path AC count should approach or exceed 15, triggering the cap warning
The crew should scope to the narrowest useful first slice (e.g. ghost-score distribution only)

reference_story.title: Dashboard – Ghost Score Distribution View
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to see the distribution of ghost scores across my analyzed postings, so that I can understand the overall quality of jobs I'm finding.

acs.name: Distribution Chart Displayed
acs.given: a job seeker has analyzed at least one posting
thens: A bar chart will show the distribution of ghost scores across all analyzed postings.
The chart will group scores into buckets (0-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-80, 81-100).

acs.name: No Analyzed Postings
acs.given: a job seeker has not analyzed any postings
thens: An empty state will be shown: "Analyze some postings to see your score distribution."

assumptions_carried: A1 — This story covers ghost-score distribution only; trends, analytics, and application success rates are separate stories.
A2 — The chart is read-only; no filtering or drill-down in this scope.
A3 — Score data is pulled from the existing Supabase store; no new data collection needed.

golden_set.notes: A well-behaved crew narrows this to one slice and explicitly names the rest as out-of-scope. Scope fidelity is the primary rubric dimension being tested.

expected_behaviors: The ask is too vague to produce a meaningful story
Researcher finds nothing targeted to research
Analyst should flag massive ambiguity — everything is assumption
Writer should produce a heavily PLACEHOLDERed story or the crew should surface that the ask needs clarification
Grounding and completeness scores should be LOW — this is correct behavior

reference_story.title: [Feature Name] – [Story Name] (PLACEHOLDER)
reference_story.story: As a [role to be confirmed], I want [action to be confirmed — the ask 'make it better' does not specify a capability], so that [outcome to be confirmed by PM].

acs.name: Core Behavior (Unspecified)
acs.given: a [role to be confirmed] performs the undefined action
thens: The described capability will behave as specified — pending PM clarification of 'make it better'.

acs.name: Review Gate
acs.given: this story was generated from an ambiguous ask
thens: The PM will define the specific capability before this story is committed.

assumptions_carried: A1 — The ask does not specify a feature, user role, or success criterion.
A2 — Every field in this story requires PM clarification before commitment.

golden_set.notes: This tests the crew's honesty under ambiguity. A good crew does not confidently invent a feature from 'make it better.' It should maximally flag, minimally invent.

golden_set.ask: The ghost score should also factor in the company's Glassdoor rating, LinkedIn headcount trend, and whether the company has posted on Indeed in the last 30 days.
expected_behaviors: Researcher identifies the three existing signals (C2) but notes that Glassdoor, LinkedIn, and Indeed integrations do not exist
Analyst should flag each external data source as a separate dependency/spike — not something to build in one story
Analyst should scope to one signal at a time or flag the whole ask as an epic needing decomposition
Writer should not produce ACs that assume these integrations exist
The crew defends against the 'invented scope' failure mode here

reference_story.title: Ghost Score – Additional Signal Sources (Spike Recommended)
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want the ghost score to incorporate additional signals beyond the current three, so that the prediction is more accurate.

acs.name: New Signal Integrated
acs.given: a new signal source has been validated and integrated
thens: The ghost score will incorporate the new signal alongside the existing three.
The evidence panel will display the new signal's contribution.

acs.name: Signal Source Unavailable
acs.given: an external data source is unreachable at analysis time
thens: The score will be computed using available signals only.
The evidence panel will note which signals were unavailable.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Glassdoor, LinkedIn, and Indeed each require separate API integrations that do not exist today — each is a spike.
A2 — Signal weighting and recalibration are required when adding new sources — a separate ML task.
A3 — This story assumes one signal is added at a time; the ask names three, which is likely an epic.

golden_set.notes: Tests whether the crew avoids treating three unbuilt integrations as in-scope for one story. The correct move is to flag as a spike or epic.

golden_set.ask: The Analyze page should show when the posting was first seen.
expected_behaviors: Researcher identifies posting age is already computed in features.sql (C2, C3)
Analyst scopes to displaying existing data — no new computation needed
This is a small, well-grounded ask that should produce a clean 2-3 AC story
Completeness score should note this is appropriately small — no need for many ACs

reference_story.title: Analyze – Show First-Seen Date
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to see when a posting was first detected by AutoApply, so that I can gauge how long it has been open.

acs.name: First-Seen Date Displayed
acs.given: a job seeker has analyzed a posting
thens: The posting's first-seen date will be shown in the evidence panel.
The date will be formatted as a relative label (e.g. "First seen 23 days ago") with the absolute date on hover.

acs.name: First-Seen Unknown
acs.given: the posting was not tracked from its original appearance
thens: The first-seen field will show "Unknown — first tracked [date]" using the earliest record available.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Posting age data from features.sql is surfaced as a user-facing date, not just a classifier input.

golden_set.ask: Let users set up a daily email digest of new postings matching their search criteria.
expected_behaviors: Researcher identifies the icebox email digest item (C6) as adjacent and Resend as the assumed provider (C4)
Researcher notes no search-criteria persistence or saved-search feature exists in the corpus
Analyst flags saved searches as a dependency that does not exist
Writer should not invent a search-saving mechanism in the ACs — flag as assumption

reference_story.title: Search – Daily New-Posting Digest
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to receive a daily email digest of new postings matching my saved search criteria, so that I can stay current without checking the platform every day.

acs.name: Digest Received
acs.given: a job seeker has at least one saved search with digest enabled
thens: The job seeker will receive one email listing new postings matching their saved criteria from the past 24 hours.
Each listing will show job title, company, ghost score, and a link to the posting.

acs.name: No New Matches
acs.given: no new postings match the saved criteria
thens: No email will be sent for that day.

acs.name: Multiple Saved Searches
acs.given: a job seeker has multiple saved searches with digest enabled
thens: All matching results will be consolidated into a single email, grouped by search.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Saved searches do not exist today; that feature is a prerequisite (separate story).
A2 — Resend is the email provider (C4).
A3 — Adjacent to the icebox digest idea (C6) but distinct — this is search-based, not saved-job-based.

golden_set.ask: We need to track which jobs users apply to and whether they hear back.
expected_behaviors: The ask contains two capabilities: tracking applications and tracking responses — likely two stories
Neither capability exists in the corpus; C1 covers saved jobs but not applications
Analyst should scope to application tracking only and move response tracking to out-of-scope or a second story
Writer should not invent an email-parsing or response-detection mechanism

reference_story.title: Saved Jobs – Track Application Status
reference_story.story: As a job seeker, I want to mark a saved job as 'Applied' with the date I applied, so that I can track my application pipeline.

acs.name: Mark as Applied
acs.given: a job seeker is viewing a saved job
thens: The job's status will change to "Applied".
Today's date will be recorded as the application date.
The job will move to an "Applied" section on the History page.

acs.name: Already Applied
acs.given: a job seeker has already marked a job as Applied
thens: The button will show "Applied on [date]" and will not allow a duplicate entry.

assumptions_carried: A1 — Application tracking is a manual action (user clicks a button); not automated detection.
A2 — Response tracking ('did they hear back') is a separate story — scoped out of this one.
A3 — Requires a status field on saved_jobs (schema change, same dependency as snooze in G03).

golden_set.notes: Tests whether the crew splits the compound ask and avoids inventing a response-tracking mechanism.
